questions.question: Why does Cortex group related security information into cases?
options: To organize issues, assets, artifacts, and investigation context around a security event
To prevent analysts from viewing individual issues after correlation
To move issue data into long-term storage before triage
To replace issue severity with only asset criticality
correct_answers: To organize issues, assets, artifacts, and investigation context around a security event

questions.question: What does the Key Assets & Artifacts tab help analysts review?
options: Hosts, users, and notable artifacts associated with the case
Only the playbook task execution graph for the case
Only the licensing details for endpoint data collection
The global list of all integrations installed in the tenant
correct_answers: Hosts, users, and notable artifacts associated with the case

questions.question: What is the practical effect of case thresholds?
options: They define when a case should stop accepting additional issues
They prevent issues from being assigned a severity
They determine which artifacts are sent to WildFire
They disable case comments after a case is assigned
correct_answers: They define when a case should stop accepting additional issues

questions.question: How do external integrations improve case investigations?
options: They enrich investigation context with information from external security sources
They automatically close every issue that joins an existing case
They replace Cortex case fields with integration-specific fields
They prevent analysts from changing a case status manually
correct_answers: They enrich investigation context with information from external security sources

questions.question: Which view is most useful when an analyst needs a consolidated case summary plus related tabs for investigation data?
options: The case details pane
The XQL query editor
The endpoint policy profile editor
The content pack version history view
correct_answers: The case details pane

questions.question: A case contains multiple issues tied to related assets and artifacts. What is the main benefit of this grouping?
options: It gives analysts a more complete view of the security event and its impact
It removes the need to preserve individual issue evidence
It converts every issue into a separate standalone incident
It forces every asset to use the same remediation action
correct_answers: It gives analysts a more complete view of the security event and its impact

questions.question: Which outcome best describes effective case management in Cortex?
options: Faster investigation through organized evidence, related issues, and actionable context
Reduced visibility by separating artifacts from issue data
Automated deletion of issues after the first investigation step
Manual recreation of all endpoint and artifact relationships
correct_answers: Faster investigation through organized evidence, related issues, and actionable context

questions.question: Which components are central to how Cortex organizes incident information into cases?
options: Cases, issues, assets, and artifacts
Queries, dashboards, widgets, and reports
Jobs, feeds, schedules, and recurrence intervals
Lists, commands, indicators, and context keys
correct_answers: Cases, issues, assets, and artifacts

questions.question: What does issue matching help Cortex do?
options: Associate new issues with an existing case when matching criteria are met
Assign every issue to a new case even when related cases exist
Remove issue attributes before displaying them in the case list
Apply the same score to all cases regardless of evidence
correct_answers: Associate new issues with an existing case when matching criteria are met

questions.question: Why would an analyst use case actions while working a case?
options: To update, manage, or progress the case based on investigation findings
To prevent any additional issues from being displayed in Cortex
To convert the case into a static report before triage
To remove all scoring logic from the tenant
correct_answers: To update, manage, or progress the case based on investigation findings

questions.question: What is the purpose of detail view tabs in a case?
options: To separate and organize investigation information such as overview, issues, artifacts, and related details
To hide case information from analysts until a playbook finishes
To display only historical dashboard widgets
To configure endpoint policy enforcement
correct_answers: To separate and organize investigation information such as overview, issues, artifacts, and related details

questions.question: How do case scoring rules support analysts?
options: They help evaluate and prioritize cases based on defined scoring logic
They delete cases that fall below a defined severity
They replace artifact enrichment with manual notes
They prevent related issues from binding to a case
correct_answers: They help evaluate and prioritize cases based on defined scoring logic

questions.question: An issue matches an existing case. What action best preserves investigation continuity?
options: Bind the issue to the matching case
Delete the issue and create a note
Export the issue and remove it from Cortex
Disable the case scoring rule
correct_answers: Bind the issue to the matching case

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Case ID in the Issues table?
options: It helps analysts identify which case an issue is associated with
It replaces the issue's external ID
It indicates whether endpoint isolation is enabled
It shows the name of the assigned playbook only
correct_answers: It helps analysts identify which case an issue is associated with

questions.question: Which objects are common across issue handling in Cortex?
options: Issue, case, and log
Feed, job, and recurrence
Dashboard, report, and widget
Script, Docker image, and timeout
correct_answers: Issue, case, and log

questions.question: Why do issue attributes matter during triage?
options: They provide context analysts use to understand, prioritize, and act on issues
They replace causality data with a static severity label
They are used only after an issue is closed
They prevent Cortex from linking issues to cases
correct_answers: They provide context analysts use to understand, prioritize, and act on issues

questions.question: Which issue action helps an analyst examine the sequence of related events?
options: Investigate Causality Chain
Create list
Pause job
Revert content pack
correct_answers: Investigate Causality Chain

questions.question: What are issue starring rules used for?
options: Prioritizing issues based on defined policies
Suppressing all network alerts globally
Changing the case threshold timer
Running a feed-triggered playbook
correct_answers: Prioritizing issues based on defined policies

questions.question: How do featured issue fields help focus investigation work?
options: They surface selected values that can influence issue priority and analyst attention
They remove issue JSON from the issue details pane
They prevent the issue from being starred
They disable causality and timeline investigation
correct_answers: They surface selected values that can influence issue priority and analyst attention

questions.question: What does a stitched issue provide that is useful for deeper investigation?
options: Additional linked causality or event context related to the issue
A guarantee that no endpoint data is associated with the issue
A replacement for all issue actions
A static report that cannot be expanded
correct_answers: Additional linked causality or event context related to the issue

questions.question: When would an analyst use pivots from an issue?
options: To move from issue details into related views for deeper investigation
To remove the issue from all cases
To convert the issue into a scheduled query
To disable featured issue fields
correct_answers: To move from issue details into related views for deeper investigation

questions.question: What is the main role of a Cortex War Room?
options: To provide a collaborative space for investigation activity, artifacts, notes, and commands
To replace all case fields with static comments
To store only dashboard reports
To configure global exception profiles
correct_answers: To provide a collaborative space for investigation activity, artifacts, notes, and commands

questions.question: Which set of actions can be performed on War Room entries?
options: Mark as note, view artifact in a new tab, attach to task, download artifact, and add tags
Pause job, resume job, abort job, and delete job
Create IOC, import BIOC, revert content pack, and update list
Disable endpoint, isolate network, edit license, and purge logs
correct_answers: Mark as note, view artifact in a new tab, attach to task, download artifact, and add tags

questions.question: What can analysts execute from the Cortex CLI?
options: Automation scripts, integration commands, and collaboration commands
Only dashboard widget exports
Only case scoring formulas
Only Marketplace update checks
correct_answers: Automation scripts, integration commands, and collaboration commands

questions.question: Which CLI feature helps analysts find commands faster while typing?
options: Auto-complete
Case binding
Issue starring
Chart panel
correct_answers: Auto-complete

questions.question: Why is context data useful in Cortex investigations?
options: It stores structured investigation data that commands, automations, and playbooks can reference
It prevents commands from returning output
It stores only analyst usernames
It deletes artifacts after download
correct_answers: It stores structured investigation data that commands, automations, and playbooks can reference

questions.question: When reviewing a War Room artifact, why might an analyst attach it to a task?
options: To connect relevant evidence to a specific investigation or response step
To hide it from the War Room entry list
To convert it into an endpoint policy
To mark the case as closed automatically
correct_answers: To connect relevant evidence to a specific investigation or response step

questions.question: What is a practical benefit of filtering War Room entries?
options: It helps analysts focus on relevant notes, commands, artifacts, or activity during an investigation
It permanently deletes nonmatching entries
It disables integration commands
It removes context data from the case
correct_answers: It helps analysts focus on relevant notes, commands, artifacts, or activity during an investigation

questions.question: What is the Causality View designed to help analysts understand?
options: The causal relationships and investigation context behind an issue
The list of scheduled jobs for a tenant
The version history of installed content packs
The available columns in Query Center
correct_answers: The causal relationships and investigation context behind an issue

questions.question: Why are stitched issues valuable in causality analysis?
options: They provide richer linked information for causal and timeline investigation
They remove all event details from the issue
They disable process node shortcut actions
They prevent timeline analysis from opening
correct_answers: They provide richer linked information for causal and timeline investigation

questions.question: What does a causality instance graph represent?
options: Connected nodes and events that form the activity chain for an issue
A list of all imported indicators
A scheduled query run history
A content pack dependency tree
correct_answers: Connected nodes and events that form the activity chain for an issue

questions.question: What do process node shortcut menu actions enable?
options: Investigation or response actions from the context of a selected process
Editing case SLA thresholds
Creating list version history entries
Changing the query schedule type
correct_answers: Investigation or response actions from the context of a selected process

questions.question: How does Timeline View complement causality analysis?
options: It lets analysts review event data over time for the issue
It replaces all causal graph nodes with static text
It is used only to create exclusions
It suppresses all related endpoint events
correct_answers: It lets analysts review event data over time for the issue

questions.question: If a non-stitched issue has limited information, what should an analyst expect?
options: Some causality or investigation details may be unavailable compared with stitched issues
The issue will always contain a complete process tree
All shortcut menu actions will become mandatory
Timeline analysis will automatically close the case
correct_answers: Some causality or investigation details may be unavailable compared with stitched issues

questions.question: What is an attack region in a causality chain useful for?
options: Focusing investigation on the portion of the chain most relevant to suspicious activity
Changing job trigger frequency
Importing external lists into Cortex
Reverting an installed content pack
correct_answers: Focusing investigation on the portion of the chain most relevant to suspicious activity

questions.question: What is the purpose of log stitching in Cortex?
options: To correlate logs and issues so analysts can use causality chains and timelines
To delete raw endpoint telemetry after issue creation
To convert every log into a manual task
To disable machine learning analytics
correct_answers: To correlate logs and issues so analysts can use causality chains and timelines

questions.question: Which data types are associated with enhanced endpoint data collection?
options: Process operations and network operations
Only dashboard widgets and reports
Only list names and list data
Only query templates and query schedules
correct_answers: Process operations and network operations

questions.question: Which fields are used when checking stitching status?
options: matching_status and agent_data_collection_status
case_score and case_weight
listName and listData
job_type and recurrence_interval
correct_answers: matching_status and agent_data_collection_status

questions.question: How does the Analytics Engine identify suspicious behavior?
options: It models normal behavior with machine learning and detects deviations or suspicious patterns
It only compares files against manually imported allow lists
It disables behavioral analytics when issues are stitched
It relies only on case scoring rules
correct_answers: It models normal behavior with machine learning and detects deviations or suspicious patterns

questions.question: Why is MITRE ATT&CK coverage relevant to integrated analysis?
options: It helps map detector coverage and suspicious behavior to recognized attack tactics
It defines how lists are imported from local files
It controls whether War Room commands can run
It decides which content packs can be deleted
correct_answers: It helps map detector coverage and suspicious behavior to recognized attack tactics

questions.question: What can analysts do with stitched issues in the Issues table?
options: Open related investigative views such as the card or timeline when data is available
Only export the issue to a local spreadsheet
Only convert the issue into a scheduled query
Only disable endpoint data collection
correct_answers: Open related investigative views such as the card or timeline when data is available

questions.question: What is the relationship between issues and logs in integrated analysis?
options: Logs provide event context that can be correlated with issues for deeper investigation
Logs are discarded once an issue is generated
Issues are stored only as raw logs without enrichment
Logs can be viewed only from list commands
correct_answers: Logs provide event context that can be correlated with issues for deeper investigation

questions.question: Which set describes Cortex response action categories?
options: Instant Response, Further Investigation, and Maintenance and Administration
Issue Matching, Case Scoring, and Case Thresholds
Time Triggered, Feed Triggered, and Manual Jobs
Template Query, XQL Query, and Query Helper
correct_answers: Instant Response, Further Investigation, and Maintenance and Administration

questions.question: Which targets can response actions apply to?
options: Processes and files, endpoints, and networks
Only cases and dashboards
Only lists and commands
Only reports and widgets
correct_answers: Processes and files, endpoints, and networks

questions.question: What transport is associated with server-initiated actions?
options: WebSocket
SMTP relay
Local file upload
DOCX media extraction
correct_answers: WebSocket

questions.question: What is the Action Center used for?
options: Performing and tracking response actions
Building scheduled XQL queries
Editing issue matching thresholds
Managing list version history
correct_answers: Performing and tracking response actions

questions.question: Which response actions are specifically associated with endpoint response work?
options: Run Live Terminal and isolate an endpoint
Create scoring rules and case layouts
Import list items and view version history
Create periodic and non-periodic scheduled queries
correct_answers: Run Live Terminal and isolate an endpoint

questions.question: Why is limiting access to response actions important?
options: Response actions can affect endpoints, processes, files, or networks and should be controlled
Response actions are only visual labels with no operational effect
All users must always be able to isolate endpoints
Access controls prevent issues from being generated
correct_answers: Response actions can affect endpoints, processes, files, or networks and should be controlled

questions.question: What does a failover to HTTP option support for server-initiated actions?
options: Alternative communication if the preferred live session path is unavailable
Automatic deletion of failed actions
Conversion of actions into case scoring rules
Export of all response actions to a list
correct_answers: Alternative communication if the preferred live session path is unavailable

questions.question: What are remediation suggestions used for?
options: Presenting recommended actions analysts can take to remediate detected issues
Building query templates for recurring hunts
Creating case scoring rules from artifact fields
Replacing all manual response actions with exclusions
correct_answers: Presenting recommended actions analysts can take to remediate detected issues

questions.question: Which set contains examples of remediation suggestion actions?
options: Delete, restore, or rename file; delete or restore registry value; terminate causality
Create scheduled query; edit dataset; save query template
Create list; import list; view list version history
Open dashboard; export report; add widget
correct_answers: Delete, restore, or rename file; delete or restore registry value; terminate causality

questions.question: What is a key purpose of remote script execution?
options: Running custom scripts on endpoints and tracking execution status
Replacing issue causality graphs with static notes
Disabling all endpoint response actions
Automatically closing every case with a registry value
correct_answers: Running custom scripts on endpoints and tracking execution status

questions.question: Which task is performed from the Scripts Library workflow?
options: Uploading ready-to-use Python scripts or adding a new script
Binding issues to cases with matching rules
Creating a scheduled query from Query Center
Viewing the case details pane
correct_answers: Uploading ready-to-use Python scripts or adding a new script

questions.question: What does the Cortex EDL service help manage?
options: External dynamic lists of IP addresses and domain names
Case detail tabs and scoring rules
War Room command auto-complete
Scheduled query recurrence intervals
correct_answers: External dynamic lists of IP addresses and domain names

questions.question: Why would an analyst track remediation status?
options: To verify whether suggested or initiated remediation actions completed successfully
To suppress all future issues from the same endpoint
To convert a remediation suggestion into a report widget
To remove the related issue from all cases
correct_answers: To verify whether suggested or initiated remediation actions completed successfully

questions.question: What is the benefit of performing remediation actions in bulk?
options: It allows the same remediation action to be applied efficiently across multiple relevant items
It forces each item to be investigated in a separate tenant
It disables manual remediation options
It prevents remediation status from being tracked
correct_answers: It allows the same remediation action to be applied efficiently across multiple relevant items

questions.question: Which capabilities contribute to Cortex threat detection strategy?
options: Threat visibility, behavioral analytics, endpoint protection, network security integration, investigation, and threat intelligence
Only case scoring, dashboard widgets, and report exports
Only list commands and War Room notes
Only content pack deletion and version history
correct_answers: Threat visibility, behavioral analytics, endpoint protection, network security integration, investigation, and threat intelligence

questions.question: Which MITRE ATT&CK tactics are listed as part of threat coverage?
options: Execution, Persistence, Discovery, Lateral Movement, Command and Control, and Exfiltration
Create, Read, Update, Delete, Search, and Export
Time Triggered, Feed Triggered, Manual, Paused, Disabled, and Error
Inline, Out-of-Band, None, Manual, Automatic, and Built-in
correct_answers: Execution, Persistence, Discovery, Lateral Movement, Command and Control, and Exfiltration

questions.question: What is the difference between an IOC and a BIOC at a high level?
options: An IOC represents a threat indicator, while a BIOC represents suspicious behavior patterns
An IOC is a dashboard widget, while a BIOC is a report widget
An IOC is used only for jobs, while a BIOC is used only for lists
An IOC closes a case, while a BIOC creates a case threshold
correct_answers: An IOC represents a threat indicator, while a BIOC represents suspicious behavior patterns

questions.question: What are Correlation Rules used for in detection?
options: Finding patterns across events that can indicate threats and generate issues
Importing lists from local files
Managing case detail view tabs
Running Live Terminal on endpoints
correct_answers: Finding patterns across events that can indicate threats and generate issues

questions.question: How does network security analytics support Cortex detections?
options: It adds network activity visibility that can reveal suspicious behavior or attack patterns
It replaces all endpoint telemetry with user notes
It prevents correlation rules from generating issues
It is used only for report formatting
correct_answers: It adds network activity visibility that can reveal suspicious behavior or attack patterns

questions.question: Why are detection rule use cases important?
options: They define the security scenario or behavior a detection rule is meant to identify
They determine which DOCX images are embedded in a lesson
They assign every alert to the same analyst
They replace incident investigation with a static list
correct_answers: They define the security scenario or behavior a detection rule is meant to identify

questions.question: What is the relationship between analytics use cases and issue generation?
options: Analytics identify suspicious activity and can generate issues for investigation
Analytics suppress all issues by default
Analytics only change case scoring values
Analytics are used only to import threat feeds
correct_answers: Analytics identify suspicious activity and can generate issues for investigation

questions.question: Which rule types are part of the Basic Rules lesson content?
options: IOC, BIOC, Custom Prevention, suppression, and correlation rules
Case scoring, detail tab, and case threshold rules only
List import, list export, and list version rules only
Job recurrence and feed monitoring rules only
correct_answers: IOC, BIOC, Custom Prevention, suppression, and correlation rules

questions.question: What are IOC rules based on?
options: Indicators of compromise used as custom threat indicators
Job execution state changes
Case detail tab selections
War Room note formatting
correct_answers: Indicators of compromise used as custom threat indicators

questions.question: What do BIOC rules focus on?
options: Behavioral indicators that identify suspicious activity patterns
Static report widgets in dashboards
Case comments created by analysts
Local files imported into a list
correct_answers: Behavioral indicators that identify suspicious activity patterns

questions.question: When would suppression rules be useful?
options: When known IOC or BIOC matches should be suppressed to reduce unwanted detections
When every endpoint response action should be forced to run
When case detail tabs need to be reordered
When a scheduled query needs to run weekly
correct_answers: When known IOC or BIOC matches should be suppressed to reduce unwanted detections

questions.question: How can lookup datasets be managed in relation to correlation rules?
options: Through correlation rules and APIs
Only through War Room notes
Only through endpoint isolation actions
Only by deleting content packs
correct_answers: Through correlation rules and APIs

questions.question: What is a Custom Prevention Rule intended to do?
options: Define custom prevention logic for specified suspicious or unwanted activity
Create dashboard widgets from case details
Schedule a playbook to run on a feed
Assign every issue to a new case
correct_answers: Define custom prevention logic for specified suspicious or unwanted activity

questions.question: Why are datasets relevant to rule matching?
options: They provide lookup data that rules can reference while evaluating events
They replace all issue attributes with attachments
They are used only to store exported screenshots
They determine whether a case can be scored
correct_answers: They provide lookup data that rules can reference while evaluating events

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of an issue exclusion?
options: Suppressing expected or noisy issues so analysts can focus on relevant detections
Disabling a protection module on selected endpoints
Running a remediation script from the Action Center
Creating a scheduled query from Query Builder
correct_answers: Suppressing expected or noisy issues so analysts can focus on relevant detections

questions.question: What do exceptions affect?
options: Protection modules
Case detail tabs
Query templates
War Room note filters
correct_answers: Protection modules

questions.question: How do exceptions profiles help manage exceptions?
options: They organize exception settings so they can be applied and managed consistently
They convert exclusions into correlation rules
They automatically close every case with excluded issues
They remove the need to audit exclusions
correct_answers: They organize exception settings so they can be applied and managed consistently

questions.question: Which statement best differentiates an exclusion from an exception?
options: An exclusion suppresses issues, while an exception disables or modifies protection behavior
An exclusion creates issues, while an exception creates dashboards
An exclusion runs a script, while an exception runs a query
An exclusion manages lists, while an exception manages reports
correct_answers: An exclusion suppresses issues, while an exception disables or modifies protection behavior

questions.question: Which practices support healthy exclusion management?
options: Review, scope, audit, and consolidate exclusions
Disable all protection modules globally
Convert exclusions into case scoring rules
Delete related issues without review
correct_answers: Review, scope, audit, and consolidate exclusions

questions.question: Why is scoping exclusions important?
options: It limits suppression to the intended conditions and reduces the chance of hiding real threats
It forces every issue to be excluded globally
It disables exceptions profiles
It replaces audit review with automatic deletion
correct_answers: It limits suppression to the intended conditions and reduces the chance of hiding real threats

questions.question: What is the risk of poorly managed exclusions?
options: Important detections may be suppressed unintentionally
All endpoint protection modules become enabled
Case details become read-only
Correlation rules stop supporting lookup datasets
correct_answers: Important detections may be suppressed unintentionally

questions.question: What is a lead in the context of investigation?

A completed case that cannot accept new issues
A disabled endpoint response action
A list item imported from a local file

Managing endpoint response actions
Creating EDL domain lists
Reviewing case War Room artifacts

IOC rules and BIOC rules
Time-triggered jobs and feed-triggered jobs
Instant response actions and further investigation actions

questions.question: What is Query Center used for?

Editing case scoring rules
Managing EDL IP lists only

To convert a lead into an endpoint policy
